title: Do PROMs detect improvements in patients' knee function after Total-Knee Arthroplasty?
summary: Patients who are already scheduled to receive a Total-Knee Arthroplasty will be observed using wearable inertial movement units  for three days, to measure their performance-based knee function, two weeks before their operation. This observation will be accompanied by the answering of patient-reported outcome measures  to ascertain how each patient subjectively evaluates their own disease. Additionally their leg axis will be determined with the use of X-ray imaging. The same process with inertial movement units tracking, patient-reported outcome measures answering and leg axis determination will be repeated six weeks after the Total-Knee Arthroplasty to observe how and if the measurements and subjective answers will change. The main purpose is to determine how close the preoperative performance-based knee function is a predictor of the postoperative performance-based knee function, if the patient-reported outcome measures can detect the change in performance-based knee function and if the change in knee axis has an influence on the postoperative performance-based knee function.

interventions.name: There will be a single group of patients who will receive the same monitoring with the use of wearable inertial movement units, as well as  the intervention will be a Total-Knee Arthroplasty, for which the patients are already scheduled.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria includes meeting the requirements for a Total Knee Arthroplasty in the DGOU-Leitlinien, no comorbidities that would negatively affect participants knee function, completing the pre-operative examination in the ambulatory facilities of Oberlinklinik Potsdam, and informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria will include previous operations changing the leg axis and comorbidities that decrease the expected knee function or activity level.
